chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Lee Young versus Lester Young
summary: Collins says Lee Young was a good drummer with a businessman's sense of being in the right place, while Prez was all music.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: So any way we did have a very -- we had a kinship, we were very close. Which I can't say for his brother and I, but --
Well you worked together for a long time
Well, we worked together for a long time, but Lee was a fine drummer, fine musician. But they were -- it's a funny thing. He and Lester were alike in a lot of ways and in many ways they weren't.
He's always seemed like it to me.
Yeah, but Lee is -- how can I put this -- Lee likes to be at the right place at the right time. Okay.
Yes. You've got to take advantage of (inaudible) when he's there. He's a businessman.

Yeah. And if he's not -- that's right, and if he's not in the right place he'll leave right away, you know. Okay? So there's a difference, you know. But Prez was just all music. Music was the thing, you know. And that was it, and with Lee it was a little more business attached to it than with Prez.
